basis: Congenital lip fistulae and cleft lip/palate define this oral malformation syndrome.
Pathological neovascularization of the iris is an ocular disorder.
Infantile parkinsonism, dystonia and developmental impairment define the disease; constipation and reflux do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Limb subcutaneous fat loss and insulin resistance define disease; hypertension and hepatic steatosis are separately diagnosed metabolic complications.
Benign dermal tumors; definition explicitly excludes systemic organ involvement.
Mature B-cell malignancy; lymphoma requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis. No common extranodal site is specified.
Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency; neurological injury depends on delayed treatment and is not universal across this umbrella.
Ovarian germ-cell tumor arises in a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement is specified.
Skeletal muscle chloride-channel disorder causing myotonia and hypertrophy; no primary nerve or central nervous system disease.
Congenital cataracts, renal tubular necrosis and severe encephalopathy define the syndrome and occurred in both reported infants.
Cataracts and abnormal oral frenula define disease; cavernous vascular tumors occur in 30-79%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Benign tumor arising from hepatocytes; the endocrine-neoplasm ancestor does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Direct lung injury from aspirated or inhaled fatty substances; chemical pneumonitis does not establish infection or an immune-mediated disease.
Acute malignancy of marrow myeloid cells; no common direct extramedullary organ damage is established.
Anterior horn cell degeneration and motor axonal disease define the condition; muscle wasting and foot deformities are secondary to denervation.
Umbrella of infantile interstitial lung disorders; no additional organ involvement applies across the group.
Spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid leakage causes intracranial CSF volume loss and neurological dysfunction.
Developmental disability defines disease; dental anomalies, strabismus and cardiovascular malformations each occur in 30-79%. Facial appearance alone adds no axis.
Glioneuronal neoplasm arising in the central nervous system, usually near the fourth ventricle.
Lipodystrophy, intellectual disability and deafness define disease; osteopenia and abnormal long bones occur in 80-99%. Subcutaneous fat loss omitted under four-axis cap.
Benign vascular tumor arising in and occupying the rectum; both rectal location and blood-vessel origin define it.
Recurrent upper-airway obstruction defines disease; cardiovascular complications are separately diagnosed conditions, and somnolence is a symptom.
Inherited lipid biosynthesis disorder umbrella; neurological, muscle, skin and cardiac damage varies by subtype without a shared established frequency.
Ectodermal disease defined by skin changes and missing or abnormal teeth; hair, sweat-gland and nail abnormalities share the dermatologic axis.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay are nearly universal; obesity in 6/18 is a separate condition, and facial dysmorphism does not establish organ damage.
